thornbreak.name: Thornbreak
thornbreak.description: A muddy, thriving frontier town of ~2,000 souls, built at the crossroads of three ancient trade routes. Wood-and-stone buildings huddle around a central market square where a cracked fountain — dry for decades — serves as the town notice board. Three inns compete for travelers, a temple of the Open Door offers shelter, and a converted dwarven signal tower serves as the watch post. The palisade wall is patched in a dozen places. Thornbreak is nominally human-governed but functionally neutral ground — a place where freeholds meet, trade, spy, and pretend to get along. The air smells of smoke, horse, rain, and opportunity.

whisperwood.name: The Whisperwood
whisperwood.description: A dense, ancient forest north of Thornbreak. The trees are old and thick, their canopies so dense the forest floor lies in permanent twilight. Local stories claim the wood remembers things — old battles, old bargains, old blood. Animals act strangely near its heart. A decade ago, a hermit named Elder Heston lived at its edge, but he vanished three months ago. The settlement of Forest's Edge sits at the wood's southern border, two days north of Thornbreak by foot.

sunken_quarry.name: The Sunken Quarry
sunken_quarry.description: An abandoned dwarven excavation site an hour east of Thornbreak. The quarry was worked for fifty years, then abandoned abruptly twenty years ago — officially due to a cave-in. Locals tell different stories: something was unearthed, something was sealed, something was taken. The entrance is now a collapsed pit half-filled with brackish water. At night, some claim to see a faint blue glow from its depths. The dwarf smith Grenda Ironboot knows more than she says.

old_forest_road.name: The Old Forest Road
old_forest_road.description: The western route from Thornbreak, winding toward the elven freeholds. A well-maintained road of fitted stone, ancient and unnervingly quiet. Elven patrols are rare but efficient. The road sees less traffic than it should — the elves discourage casual travel into their territory. Fox traveled this road when he left his homeland three years ago.

iron_highway.name: The Iron Highway
iron_highway.description: The eastern route toward the dwarven holds. A broad, packed-gravel road built for heavy trade wagons — ore east, finished goods west. Dwarven merchant caravans pass through Thornbreak regularly, their drivers stoic and watchful. The road is safe enough near town but grows lawless farther east, where bandits prey on isolated shipments.

kings_run.name: The King's Run
kings_run.description: The southern road, connecting Thornbreak to the human city-leagues. A dirt road that turns to mud in spring, lined with farmsteads that grow sparser as you approach the town. Baron Aldric Vane, a human noble with territorial ambitions, has been sending armed surveyors north along this road, claiming Thornbreak's outlying lands belong to his barony by old charter. Tensions simmer.

forests_edge.name: Forest's Edge
forests_edge.description: A small logging settlement two days north of Thornbreak, at the southern border of the Whisperwood. Home to about sixty souls — woodcutters, trappers, their families. A wooden palisade, a common hall, a tiny shrine. Ten days ago, trade stopped. No messengers, no wagons, no smoke. The last traveler to visit reported an eerie silence and an unlit hearth.

longbow_arthur.name: Longbow (yew, elven make)
longbow_arthur.description: A fine elven longbow of dark yew, recurved at the tips, strung with silvery sinew. Fox's father gave it to him on his 80th birthday — 'so you can shoot straight when you inevitably stray.' It's a good bow, well-balanced, and has seen three years of use on the frontier. Fletchings are grey goose feather, marked with Fox's personal sigil: a crescent moon and a single star.

shortsword_arthur.name: Shortsword (frontier steel)
shortsword_arthur.description: A practical shortsword, bought in a Thornbreak market, unadorned but well-forged. The grip is wrapped in worn leather. It's not elven silver-steel — it's frontier honesty, meant to be used and sharpened. There's a small nick near the hilt from a practice bout with a dwarven caravan guard that Fox nearly lost.

studded_leather_arthur.name: Studded leather armor (frontier-worn)
studded_leather_arthur.description: A well-worn studded leather jerkin, reinforced with boiled leather and iron rivets. It's seen rain, mud, blood, and campfire smoke. The elven insignia on the collar has been carefully unpicked — Fox removed it when he crossed the border, not wanting to advertise his origin. The leather has molded to his frame.

survey_journal.name: Survey journal and mapping tools
survey_journal.description: A leather-bound journal half-filled with maps, notes, sketches, and observations. Fox has been documenting the frontier — its roads, its people, its wildlife, its political moods. It's part research, part diary, part compulsion. The last few pages contain sketches of Thornbreak's layout and some notes on trade patterns. A charcoal stick, a folding ruler, and a brass compass are tucked into the journal's strap.

letter_of_introduction.name: Letter of Introduction (Elven Bureau of External Affairs)
letter_of_introduction.description: A sealed parchment bearing the silver crest of the Elven Freehold's Bureau of External Affairs. It introduces Fox Arthur as a 'student of social sciences on extended fieldwork' and requests that signatories extend him 'courtesy, safe passage, and the benefit of the doubt.' It's deliberately vague — Fox's father arranged it as a compromise between 'let him go' and 'keep him safe.' The letter opens doors, but also marks him as elven officialdom, for those who can read between the lines.

explorers_pack.name: Explorer's pack
explorers_pack.description: A sturdy backpack containing: a bedroll, a mess kit, a tinderbox, 10 torches, 10 days of rations, a waterskin, 50 feet of hempen rope, and a small sewing kit. All of it is practical, slightly worn, and carefully maintained. The pack also contains a small tin of elven tea leaves — a luxury Fox allows himself on cold mornings.

silver_piece_rik.name: Scorched silver piece (elven script)
silver_piece_rik.description: A palm-sized piece of worked silver, roughly circular, scorched black on one edge. Elven script winds around its face — old script, pre-Concord style, difficult to read. It was found by the halfling Rik in the woods north of Thornbreak a week ago, near a patch of burnt ground. Rik has kept it hidden, unsure who to trust. It smells faintly of ozone and ash.

maren_holt.name: Maren Holt
maren_holt.description: Human woman, early 40s. Innkeeper of The Wanderer's Rest — the oldest and most respected inn in Thornbreak. Widow of a caravan master who died on the Iron Highway ten years ago. She has sharp grey eyes that miss nothing, a warm laugh, and a way of refilling your cup just when you need it. She knows everyone's business and shares only what serves her. Secret: She was a courier and intelligence agent for the human city-leagues before settling down. She still has contacts, and she still reads the coded messages that pass through her inn. She genuinely likes Fox — he reminds her of herself at that age.

orin_voss.name: Captain Orin Voss
orin_voss.description: Human man, late 50s. Captain of the Thornbreak Watch. A soldier past his prime who accepted this post as semi-retirement — but the job has gotten harder each year. Grey beard, rheumy eyes, a limp from an old arrow wound. He drinks too much but is still sharper than he pretends to be. He's outmatched by the town's growing complexity — smugglers, spies, territorial claims — and he knows it. He'll welcome competent help, especially from someone like Fox who has elven training and no obvious faction ties. Secret: He's been ordered by the human city-league to keep Thornbreak 'stable' at any cost, but he's hiding a letter from Baron Vane demanding the town's surrender within the month.

kaelen_brightwood.name: Kaelen Brightwood
kaelen_brightwood.description: Half-elf, appears early 30s. A charming, learned scribe and translator who runs a small scriptorium near the market square — letters, contracts, copies, translations, maps. Warm smile, well-dressed, always has a flask of good wine to share. He arrived in Thornbreak two years ago and has made himself useful and liked. Secret: He's an agent of the elven freehold's Silent Registry — intelligence service. He's been tracking the movement of old elven relics through the frontier, particularly anything being smuggled out of elven territory. He doesn't know Fox is elven nobility — or pretends not to. He's genuinely conflicted about his assignment as he's grown to like Thornbreak.

grenda_ironboot.name: Grenda Ironboot
grenda_ironboot.description: Dwarf woman, 124 years old. Master smith, runs Ironboot Forge near the east gate. Built like a barrel, arms like tree roots, voice that could strip paint. She came to Thornbreak forty years ago when the quarry was still active and stayed when it closed. She knows everyone, outlived most of her first human friends, and has a soft spot for young people with fire in their bellies. Secret: She was a sapper in the dwarven army during the War of Three Crowns. She knows exactly what was found in the Sunken Quarry — a sealed vault of pre-Concord origin containing something the dwarven high command wanted to keep buried. She helped seal it. The blue glow means something has broken the seal.

rik.name: Rik
rik.description: Halfling, appears early 20s (halfling aging is fuzzy). A scruffy messenger and errand-runner who knows every alley, roof, and loose floorboard in Thornbreak. Wiry, quick, with a grin that could charm a coin out of a miser's pocket. Orphaned, self-raised, street-smart. He works for anyone who pays — including, unwittingly, three different factions. He worships competence and despises cruelty. He's decided Fox is interesting and has been hanging around hoping for work or stories. Secret: Rik found something in the woods north of town a week ago — a piece of worked silver with elven script on it, badly scorched. He's kept it hidden, unsure who to trust.

mother_yarrow.name: Mother Yarrow
mother_yarrow.description: Human woman, 70s. Priestess of the Open Door — the god of travelers, crossroads, and frontier hospitality. Runs a small temple near the market square that offers free meals and shelter to those in need. Frail-looking but iron-willed, with pale eyes that seem to look through you. She has lived in Thornbreak since it was a trading post of sixty people. She remembers everything. She tells stories in riddles and parables. Secret: She was once a priestess of an older faith — the faith of the Whisperwood — before the Concord. She knows what sleeps in the forest and what bargains were made to keep it sleeping. Elder Heston was her friend. She knows why he vanished, and she's afraid.

silas_crow.name: Silas the Crow
silas_crow.description: Human man, early 30s. A traveling merchant who passes through Thornbreak every two weeks with a wagon of goods — fine cloth, spices, exotic liquors, old books, odd curios. Well-dressed in dark silks, rings on every finger, a ready smile. Charismatic, clever, slippery. He stays at The Wanderer's Rest and always buys a round for the house. Everyone likes Silas. Secret: He runs a smuggling operation moving artifacts, banned texts, and fugitives across freehold borders. He's currently transporting something from elven territory to a buyer in the human city-leagues — and he's being followed. He doesn't know by whom. He'll try to befriend Fox, sensing a useful contact.

elder_heston.name: Elder Heston
elder_heston.description: Human man, 80s (missing, presumed dead). A hermit who lived at the southern edge of the Whisperwood for forty years. He was the last keeper of the old traditions — tending moss-covered boundary stones, leaving offerings at certain trees, reading the movements of birds and deer. Quiet, gentle, slightly unnerving in his familiarity with the wood. Friend of Mother Yarrow. Vanished three months ago without a trace. His walking staff — ash wood, carved with spiral patterns — was left leaning against his cabin wall, untouched.

baron_aldric_vane.name: Baron Aldric Vane
baron_aldric_vane.description: Human man, 40s. A southern noble with sharp cheekbones, cold eyes, and a velvet voice. He rules a modest barony along the King's Run, but has spent the last decade acquiring land, influence, and old charters. His claim on Thornbreak is based on a document from the Treaty era that he may have had 'rediscovered' conveniently. He has not visited Thornbreak himself — he sends surveyors, letters, and increasingly, armed escorts. His motives are unclear: simple territorial expansion, or does he know something about what lies beneath the frontier? He is patient, calculating, and dangerous from a distance.

treaty_of_gilded_falls.description: The Treaty of Gilded Falls ended the War of Three Crowns — a brutal thirty-year conflict between elven, dwarven, and human powers. The treaty established the Concord of Freeholds: autonomous territories bound by trade, shared currency, and non-aggression. Halfling mediators brokered the peace. Dragonborn legions, excluded from the treaty, still nurse territorial grievances. The treaty has held for a century — but cracks are spreading.

founding_of_thornbreak.description: Thornbreak was founded as a neutral trading post at the crossroads of three major routes. The location was chosen specifically because it didn't belong to any freehold — a strip of unclaimed frontier. The town grew from a stockade and three tents to a permanent settlement of several hundred. The old dwarven signal tower was converted into a watch post. The town's charter guarantees it as free territory under the Concord's protection — a status Baron Vane now challenges.

quarry_collapse.description: The dwarven excavation at the Sunken Quarry struck something unexpected at depth — a vault of pre-Concord construction, sealed with magic and materials the dwarven engineers didn't recognize. Before they could fully open it, a dwarven High Command courier arrived with sealed orders. The excavation was abandoned overnight. The entrance was collapsed. The crew was redistributed. Grenda Ironboot was the only one who stayed in Thornbreak, and she's never spoken of what they found — until now, when the blue glow has returned to the pit.

vanishing_of_elder_heston.description: Elder Heston, an aging human hermit who lived at the edge of the Whisperwood, vanished without a trace. He was a friend of Mother Yarrow and had been a guardian of sorts — tending the old stones at the forest's edge, keeping old traditions. Mother Yarrow was the last person to speak with him. He told her he'd heard something calling from the deep wood, something that 'shouldn't be awake yet.' Three days later, his cabin was empty — fire cold, door open, his walking staff leaning against the wall as if he'd stepped out for a moment and never returned. Mother Yarrow believes the forest took him. She hasn't said why.

barons_surveyors.description: Baron Aldric Vane began sending armed surveyors north along the King's Run, claiming by old charter that Thornbreak's territory falls within his ancestral domain. Captain Voss has intercepted three surveying parties and sent them back, but they keep coming. The most recent party carried a sealed letter demanding the town's peaceful surrender within thirty days. Voss has told no one except (privately) Maren Holt. The Baron's timing — coinciding with the Forest's Edge silence and the quarry disturbance — may be opportunistic, or coordinated.

silence_at_forests_edge.name: The Silence at Forest's Edge
silence_at_forests_edge.description: Root thread. The logging settlement of Forest's Edge, two days north of Thornbreak at the edge of the Whisperwood, has gone silent. No trade, no messages, no smoke for ten days. Last traveler reported an eerie quiet and cold hearths. Captain Voss needs someone to investigate — without drawing attention that might panic the town or alert Baron Vane's agents. Fox is a logical choice: capable, not obviously aligned with any faction. The clock is: whatever happened has already been spreading for ten days, and the Whisperwood doesn't give back what it takes.

the_sunken_secret.name: The Sunken Secret
the_sunken_secret.description: Subthread. The abandoned dwarven quarry east of Thornbreak has started showing a faint blue glow at night. Grenda Ironboot knows what was sealed there — a pre-Concord vault containing something the dwarven high command buried during the war. If the seal is breaking, it could spill trouble that makes border disputes look like a tavern brawl. The blue glow has been noticed by locals, and Silas the Crow has taken an interest.

the_smugglers_game.name: The Smuggler's Game
the_smugglers_game.description: Subthread. Silas the Crow is moving something through Thornbreak — an elven artifact of unknown nature. Kaelen Brightwood of the elven Silent Registry is tracking it. The artifact may be connected to the Whisperwood, the Sunken Quarry, or both. The handoff is scheduled within the next few days. Silas doesn't know Kaelen is an agent. Kaelen doesn't know what the artifact does. Both are circling each other, and Fox could get caught between them.

the_barons_claim.name: The Baron's Claim
the_barons_claim.description: Subthread. Baron Aldric Vane, a human noble from the southern city-leagues, has been pressing a territorial claim on Thornbreak based on a century-old charter. Surveyors have been spotted mapping the outskirts. Captain Voss has a letter demanding surrender within the month. The Baron may be using the chaos of Forest's Edge and the quarry disturbance as cover for a quiet takeover — or he may be genuinely unaware of what's brewing in the north.

log: "The elven kingdom suffocated me. Perfect gardens, perfect manners, perfect silence — a museum of ourselves. I needed to see people who argued, who made mistakes, who lived in the present instead of measuring centuries. Father said I was wasting my inheritance. Mother said I'd be back in a year. I've been gone three. Some days I miss the quiet. Most days I don't."

"The Concord is a beautiful lie. Everyone knows the truth: elves hoard their magic, dwarves their gold, humans their numbers, halflings their secrets. The peace holds because everyone is afraid of what happens if it breaks — not because anyone believes in it. That's the game, and I wanted to see it played up close."

"I've noticed Captain Voss watching me. He's testing, weighing — I've seen the look before. He needs something done that he can't trust to his own watch. I don't know what yet, but it's coming. And I have a suspicion it's connected to the forest to the north, where the birds have stopped singing."

"Thornbreak appealed to me because it's honest about what it is. It's muddy, loud, ugly, and nobody pretends to be noble. The humans run it but don't own it. Dwarves drink beside halflings. Elves pass through — though they rarely stay. It's what the Concord claims to be, in miniature. I've been here three months now, longer than anywhere else. That means something."

prior_prose:
---

# Thornbreak — Market Day, Late Autumn

The morning fog is burning off the crossroads.

You're at a corner table in **The Wanderer's Rest**, nursing a cup of tea that's gone cold. Maren Holt refills it without asking — she does that, notices things without being told — and nods toward the window. Outside, the market square is filling: a dwarven merchant arguing with a halfling spice-seller, a dragonborn scout in patched leathers haggling over horses, children chasing a runaway goat past the dry fountain.

*Three years since you left the elven kingdom. Three months since you settled here.*

Your survey journal lies open on the table, half-filled with notes on trade volumes and border markers. But you've been staring at the same page for ten minutes, because something is wrong.

The birds.

The thrushes that nest in the eaves of Maren's stable — they've been silent for three days. You noticed it yesterday morning and told yourself it was the season. But the sparrows in the square are quiet too. And the caravan master who came down from the north last night said the forest had gone still. No birdsong. No rustle in the underbrush. Just *silence*.

The door creaks open.

**Captain Orin Voss** steps in, squints across the room, and spots you. He looks tired — more than usual. He nods once, a heavy gesture, and jerks his head toward the back room. His hand rests on the letter tucked into his belt.

---

**What do you do?**

- **Rise** and follow Voss into the back room.
- **Wave him over** to your table — you'd rather talk in the open, where you can see faces.
- **Let him wait** a moment. You finish a note in your journal first, one sentence: *"Birds quiet. Forest's Edge silent ten days. Voss nervous. Something is moving."*
- **Something else?**
